title: Updater functions: build on the queued value

slides.text: Pass a function, not a value 🧮
slides.say: Want to update the same state several times in one click? Pass a function instead of a value.
n arrow n plus one is an updater function. React queues each one, then runs them in order on the next render. Zero becomes one, two, three.

slides.text: React batches: it waits until the whole handler has run, then works through the queue.
slides.say: This works because React batches. It waits until your whole event handler finishes, then processes the queue.
You can mix them. A plain value means replace with that value. The updater then builds on it. Five, plus one, gives six.

slides.text: Name the argument after the state: setEnabled(e => !e). Keep updaters pure.
slides.say: Name the argument after the state, like e for enabled. Updaters run during rendering, so keep them pure. Just return the result.
